text.p: - Slovenia's capital Ljubljana is the most expensive city of the state, Delo's research showed. In Ljubljana, basic food prices have risen 10 percent since December last year.
- Strong wind coused hefty electricity problems in the Slovenian seaside area of Koper on Wednesday.
- President Milan Kucan will continue talks with political parties on Monday, aimed at determining a candidate for a new prime minister following the general election on November 10.
- Olympic silver medallists Brigita Bukovec and Andraz Vehovar were named Slovenian sportspeople of 1996.
- Slovenian Accountancy Court, which controls public spending, found irregularities in the accounts of the Ljubljana District Court for 1995.
- The Housing Fund this week granted 3.2 billion tolars ($22.7 million) for favourable housing loans.
